'''Baba ganoush''' is a common Middle Eastern and Mediterranean dip with a creamy, somewhat smoky flavor. It is usually eaten with [[Cookbook:Pita|pita bread]] although [[Cookbook:Naan|naan]] or a crispy [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] also work well.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (1 to 1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]]) medium-large [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]], any variety
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] raw [[Cookbook:Tahini|tahini]]
* Juice of 1 [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]]  or [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Clove|clove]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], crushed
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Paprika|Paprika]] or [[Cookbook:Cayenne_pepper|cayenne pepper]], as a garnish

==Procedure==
# Roast the eggplant. This can be done in a variety of ways, but the flesh should be fully cooked and the skin should be burned and falling off easily. An effective method is to prick the eggplant and place it a few inches under a [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]], turning it as the exposed skin blackens, about every 3-4 minutes. Place a pan underneath to catch the juices, and discard them. 
# Scrape off the eggplant skin. It's alright if you miss a few burned bits.
# Finely chop or blend the eggplant flesh with the rest of the ingredients. The consistency should be smooth. Reserve a bit of the olive oil, and drizzle that over the top. Sprinkle with some paprika or cayenne.
